question: The obstetric conjugate — the shortest antero-posterior diameter of the pelvic inlet — is the direct distance from the upper border of the symphysis pubis to the sacral promontory.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. The obstetric conjugate runs from the posterior (inner) surface of the symphysis pubis, not its upper border, to the sacral promontory. The diagonal conjugate, which is measured clinically, runs from the lower border of the symphysis to the promontory.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The obstetric conjugate runs from the posterior surface of the symphysis pubis (just below the upper border) to the sacral promontory; it is approximately 10 cm. The diagonal conjugate (measured clinically) runs from the lower border of the symphysis to the promontory.
